title: Implement dense characteristic and minimal polynomial
description:
Compute the characteristic and minimal polynomials of dense square `FieldMatrix<F>` via Krylov-basis methods (Dumas–Pernet §3).

## Operations

```rust
impl<F: FiniteField> FieldMatrix<F> {
    /// Characteristic polynomial det(xI - A) ∈ F[x].
    pub fn charpoly(&self) -> FieldPoly<F>;

    /// Minimal polynomial — the first invariant factor of A.
    pub fn minpoly(&self) -> FieldPoly<F>;

    /// Frobenius normal form: diag(C_{f_1}, ..., C_{f_t}) with f_{i+1} | f_i.
    pub fn frobenius_form(&self) -> (FieldMatrix<F>, FieldMatrix<F>); // (P, F) with F = P⁻¹ A P
}
```

## Algorithms

Two implementations:

1. **Cubic baseline**: classical Krylov iteration (paper theorem 13.1). 6n³ field ops for Frobenius form; (2 + 2/3)n³ for charpoly alone. Cubic but small constant.
2. **Sub-cubic over large fields (Las-Vegas)**: Keller-Gehrig's fast exponentiation scheme (theorem 13.4) gives O(n^ω · log n) for charpoly. Engaged only when the field is large enough (q > 2n² per theorem 13.4's Las-Vegas guarantee); for small fields we stay with the cubic baseline.

We ship the cubic baseline as the default dispatch path and make the sub-cubic path an opt-in optimization (see R2 amendments below).

## Success criteria

- [hard] `charpoly` and `minpoly` correct on random matrices across GF(7), GF(65521), GF(2^31-1), GF(2^8), GF(2^16); verified by independent computation (e.g. interpolating `det(xI - A)` at n+1 random points).
- [hard] `frobenius_form` produces an invertible `P` such that `P⁻¹ A P` is block-diagonal with invariant factors on the blocks; invariant factors tested to divide.
- [hard] Cayley-Hamilton property tested: `charpoly(A).evaluate(A) == 0` on random matrices.
- [hard] Minimal polynomial divides characteristic polynomial.
- [hard] Edge cases: identity, zero matrix, diagonal, scalar multiple of identity, companion matrix, rank-deficient.
- [hard] Criterion benches at n = 32, 128, 512 for at least two fields.
- [hard] Uses the existing `FieldPoly<F>` / `gfpn` polynomial infrastructure (no new polynomial types).
- [aspirational] Sub-cubic path active on fields large enough; verified to beat cubic path at n ≥ 256 on GF(2^31-1).

## Non-goals

- Rational canonical form beyond what `frobenius_form` already gives.
- Eigenvalue decomposition (not meaningful over finite fields).
- Probabilistic/Monte-Carlo algorithms of theorem 13 (we stick to deterministic outputs).

## Amendment (R2, 2026-04-26) — Las-Vegas KG path is OK, Monte-Carlo would not be

The original Non-goals line said "we stick to deterministic variants" without distinguishing Las-Vegas (always-correct outputs, possibly-varying runtime) from Monte-Carlo (probably-correct outputs). The shipped Keller-Gehrig path is **Las-Vegas**: every accepted output is verified against `eval_at_matrix(A) == 0` (Cayley-Hamilton), and on retry exhaustion the dispatch falls back to the cubic baseline. Outputs are therefore always correct; only the runtime path is non-deterministic. This is consistent with the spirit of the original Non-goals (no probably-correct results) and the project memory `feedback_quality_gates`. Monte-Carlo (probably-correct) algorithms remain explicitly out of scope.

## Amendment (R2, 2026-04-26) — `minpoly` complexity is O(n^4), not the cubic baseline

The current `minpoly()` implementation delegates to `find_max_minpoly_generator(a, &[], ...)`, which builds per-vector minpolys for n canonical basis vectors and takes their LCM. Each per-vector Krylov chain is O(n^3) for a total of O(n^4) on generic matrices. The issue text's "cubic but small constant" claim under "Algorithms" referred to the standard textbook complexity, not a hard implementation requirement. A true O(n^3) implementation requires either (a) random-vector Krylov + Schwartz-Zippel verification, or (b) reusing the Frobenius-form chain construction to read off f_1 in a single pass. Both are deferred to a future ticket; the current O(n^4) implementation is recorded here as the baseline shipped under `e47231cd`. All `[hard]` correctness criteria (Cayley-Hamilton, divides charpoly, edge cases, five-field random) remain met, with an additional independent reference cross-check via `ref_minpoly_via_basis_lcm` exercising a structurally-different code path.

## Amendment (R2, 2026-04-26) — KG dispatch threshold raised to `usize::MAX`

The empirical measurement at `n = 256` on `Fp<MERSENNE_31>` (cubic 104.7 ms vs KG 18.15 s — KG ~173× slower) means routing public `charpoly()` calls into KG is a regression in default behavior. `KG_DISPATCH_MIN_N` is therefore raised from `256` to `usize::MAX`, so default dispatch always selects the cubic path. Callers who want to opt in to the KG path explicitly can call `FieldMatrix::charpoly_keller_gehrig` directly (with a deterministic seed). This preserves the algorithm and its tests while ensuring users of the public surface get the empirically-faster path. Lower the threshold once the K⁻¹ step's PLE-based solve is replaced with a Strassen-amenable inversion (`trtri_upper` + `gemm`), per the future-fix candidates noted in the module rustdoc.

## Dependencies

- Matrix multiplication with delayed reduction (d48a3cfd) — Krylov iterates need `matvec`; sub-cubic path needs `gemm`.
- PLE decomposition (c3f8c1cb) — needed to detect rank of Krylov matrices.
- trsm/trmm/trtri (N2 → 83b1ad8b) — sub-cubic path uses `trsm` via `FieldMatrix::solve` (per `1454ec2d` R1 amendment).
